title: a scalar where the schema wants a list
notes: The array arm of `analyze_errors`, `not isinstance(data, list)` branch, now `not_a_list_message`. `contribute:` renders as an array of `ContributeElement`, so writing the single target a user means -- `contribute: result` rather than `contribute: [result]` -- reaches it. It used to be the value pasted in front of a four-word shape assertion, `result should be a list`, in which the offending value was undelimited and indistinguishable from prose. What the golden now demonstrates, against the three defects recorded before: the value is delimited and named as a string; the expectation is stated, and so is what a list of *what* was expected, read out of the `items` the arm was about to descend into by `enumerated`; and the edit is offered. The item list says `may be` rather than `is one of` on purpose. `ContributeElement` enumerates four targets **and** admits a mapping of them to values, so `enumerated` reports the four as non-exhaustive and the wording follows -- naming them as the accepted set would have been a claim about the schema that `analyze_errors` itself would then contradict. Fix 3: `contribute: [result]` is the user's own value in a list, checked by `satisfies` against the same schema before it is offered, and executed to exit 0. Location stays 2: `prog.pdl:2` plus `  in contribute`, an excerpt and a caret, and no `:col` -- held for a separate decision at INVENTORY 7.9/7.11. The caret sits under the *key*, because that is the mark `_walk` records for a mapping entry and the value has none of its own; it carries no label for the reason `scalar_value_diagnostic` documents, that a label there would name the wrong word. Hygiene was already 3 here and stays: this reproducer's value is a bare string, so no Python `repr` ever reached the user. Give the same branch a non-scalar and one did; that is `E-SCHEMA-009-object`.
